title: FEMA is dealing with its own emergency: bed bugs | CNN Politics
text:
A turbulent week for the Department of Homeland Security now includes an infestation at the headquarters of the nation’s disaster response agency.

Bed bugs at theFederal Emergency Management Agency’s Washington, DC, hub are forcing more than 1,000 staffers at the agency to work from home Thursday while the building is fumigated, according to six sources familiar with the problem.

An agency email, which CNN reviewed, went out to staff Wednesday night warning them that the headquarters would be closed for an “urgent pest control treatment.” By Thursday, word spread that bed bugs had been found on multiple floors.

“This closure is necessary to perform a comprehensive, building-wide pest control treatment to address an active pest issue and ensure a safe, healthy workspace for all personnel,” the memo states, providing no timeline for return and adding that additional guidance will be given when the issue has been “successfully resolved.”

DHS told CNN in a statement, “this incident is currently limited to a few offices inside the building” and that the agency remains “fully operational and prepared to respond to disasters and emergencies” despite the temporary facility closure.

It’s been a tough week for Washington and government workers. The National Security Agency hasclosed its campusto most employees for three days this week as it works to restore a highly classified network used for internal communications.

And it’s not the only emergency FEMA has confronted in the past week. The infestation comes days after Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin mobilized FEMA to respond to last Friday’s nationwide ground stop when all flights were grounded because of a systems failure.

Mullin, whose department oversees FEMA, said the agency would coordinate with airports to help stranded passengers meet basic needs, including getting access to medication.

But that urgent assignment ended in roughly 24 hours and left some FEMA employees wondering why they had been summoned. Staff who were ordered to report to operations centers across the country said they received little direction and found almost nothing they could do to help, according to five agency officials who were part of the efforts.

“It was a giant waste of time and resources,” a senior FEMA official told CNN.

The deployment was part of a broader DHS response that has drawn widespreadscrutiny of Mullin. For FEMA, whose responsibilities include maintaining continuity of government and coordinating federal disaster response, it was another disruption after 22 months of upheaval.

DHS acknowledges it deployed 90 staffers and that no requests for support came in, but adds: “Suggesting that [FEMA’S] activation lacked a mission or strategy is incorrect and our mission in this incident was clear: to be ready to support state, local, tribal, and territorial partners.”

Former Homeland Security Secretary Kristi Noem and Corey Lewandowski vowed to eliminate FEMA and pushed to overhaul its operations during the first year of President Donald Trump’s second term. After their ouster, the administration sought to steady the agency under Mullin while continuing to push for shrinking the agency and forcing states to shoulder more responsibility for disaster response and recovery.

Trump nominated Cameron Hamilton to run FEMA permanently a year after Noem abruptly fired him as its acting head. Hamilton and his team faced scrutiny last month over a short-lived effort tolease two private jetsfor executive travel.
